title: What is a directory?
question: A directory is names, each pointing to a file. What happens when one is made, and when one is listed? (In memory: ramfs.)
text: A directory is names, each pointing to a file. Here one is made and the root is listed, all in memory.
1. [ramfs_mkdir](1:ramfs_mkdir) makes the new directory: an inode like a file's, and a name for it, "sub", in /.

2. Listing / with getdents64: in an in-memory file system the directory's names are the dentry cache itself, so [dcache_readdir](3:dcache_readdir) walks the children of /, and for each [filldir64](3:filldir64) copies an entry out to the program: its name, its inode number, its type. The program's line shows the names it got.
Try: make the directory twice: the second mkdirat fails with EEXIST. Or list the new, empty directory instead of /: open "/sub" and it has only "." and "..".
